input.task: What is the name of the cheapest product in the Nimbus Archive catalogue?

provenance: ADR-039 §3. The recovery half of deployed run `46883372` (see `planner-sees-a-fetch-painted-select` for that run's full record). The executor raises exactly one `semantic` failure — the identity anchor, `agent.py`'s "the value I read was not on a page about the entity you asked about" — and the recovery ladder dispatched on `locate` and `act` only, so `semantic` fell straight through to `return done(failure=cls)`. The live run therefore ended having spent 0 of its 2 replans while holding the single most actionable signal a run produces. This case is that shape on a committed fixture: plan 1 extracts `shop.html`'s first link under `anchor: "Nimbus Archive"`, a string absent from the page; plan 2 reads the fourth link under an anchor that is present. It grades three things at once — that the ladder now fires (`replans: 1`, `recovery: true`), that the planner is told WHY (`planner_note_contains` carries the anchor refusal verbatim, so the note is not a generic "a previous attempt failed"), and that the REFUSED read is not carried into the answer. The third is why the anchor check moved ahead of the `answers`/`extractions` appends: before ADR-039 the appends ran first, which was harmless only while a semantic failure ended the run on the spot. With the replan behind it, `answers` would have held `["Aurora Desk Lamp", "Cobalt Floor Rug"]` and `expect.answer` grades that it holds the second alone.

triage.red_first: RED on the pre-ADR-039 executor, restored from git for the run: `status failure:semantic`, `answer null`, `replans 0`, reason `step 2 (extract): StepError: identity anchor 'Nimbus Archive' absent from the page the answer was read from` — the deployed run's shape verbatim, checks `{status, verdict, recovery, replans, planner_note_contains}` all false.
triage.note: The laundering guard is the reason this case is not a one-word change. `drops_action and changed_nothing(rec)` refuses a replan that drops a failed action and reads the page as if it had worked; a failed EXTRACTION never changed the page and the replan after one is always a read, so the guard as written refuses every semantic replan and this case stays red with `cls in ("act", "semantic")` alone. `not reads_without_acting([step])` scopes it to a failed step that was supposed to change something. `replan-cannot-launder-noop-action` and its `extract_all` / `observe` siblings hold the direction that must not move.
